decisions.reason: As a newly launched product line that builds directly on the firm's established geospatial components and already has its own webpage, it is likely close to aspiration levels or important enough under available organisational slack to retain.

The building data digital twin service fits the firm's existing geospatial integration business and a growing market, so despite limited website prominence management would likely keep it while results remain uncertain.

Authentication and identity delegation is only close rather than central to the core offer and may face tougher evaluation, but the firm's R&D orientation and slack make continued trial more likely than withdrawal after only one year.

An open GIS application development framework is strategically close to the firm's core capabilities and, as a multi-model product line, likely supports broader solution sales, which lowers the chance of problemistic abandonment.

The explicitly announced new identity service appears intended to strengthen integration of GeoIT applications, and in a growing industry a medium-sized innovative firm would likely keep it on the market unless clear underperformance emerges.
